text:
dev-ops-sam: Hey support — our nightly CI runs started failing ~07:12 UTC with 401 invalid_api_key when hitting /v1/chat/completions. Failing job output below.

dev-ops-sam: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}] }'

dev-ops-sam: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_api_key",
    "message": "API key invalid or expired"
  }
}

emily.support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact GH Actions step or how the key is injected into the job? Any recent secret/var renames?

dev-ops-sam: Here's the workflow snippet we used (simplified):

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      REDFWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDFWOOD_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Run smoke tests
        run: ./ci/run_smoke.sh
```

maria-engineering: wait — is that env var name REDFWOOD_API_KEY (extra F) on purpose? our standard is REDWOOD_API_KEY. Did you rename the secret recently?

dev-ops-sam: ugh yes — I renamed the repo secret yesterday to REDWOOD_API_KEY while cleaning up. I updated a couple scripts but clearly missed the workflow.

dev-ops-sam: Patching workflow to use REDWOOD_API_KEY now and re-run.

dev-ops-sam: (after redeploy) quick re-run: curl returns 200 and job passes. Streaming/chat responses work again :tada:

emily.support: Great — glad that fixed it. Leaving this thread as a quick triage note: 401 in CI can be caused by env var/secret rename where the job ends up sending an empty header or an unrelated value. Suggestion: we should add a diagnostic message in our SDK/CLI when the Authorization header is missing or empty to hint at missing env var.

redwood-bot: Note added to internal ticket #4521: "CI env var mismatch (REDFWOOD_API_KEY) caused 401 invalid_api_key. Consider SDK/CLI diagnostic for missing Authorization header."

dev-ops-sam: Thanks everyone — closing on our side.
